newsitem.title: USA: MCI Q1 in line, cautions of slower growth.
newsitem.headline: MCI Q1 in line, cautions of slower growth.

text.p: MCI Communications Inc first quarter earnings were flat versus a year ago, despite a healthy rise in revenues, but it cautioned growth may slow in coming quarters as it embraces higher margin businesses.

MCI said it expects revenue and traffic growth rates to slow in coming quarters as a result of some moderation in the industry's residential market growth and MCI's strategy of investing more money in higher margin businesses.
It said these actions include continuing its shift away from carrier customers, a tightening of credit collections and transitioning to a higher-value residential customer base.

The company made the comments in conjunction with its first quarter earnings results, in which it reported net income of $0.42 per share, flat versus a year ago, and in line with the First Call consensus estimate for the quarter.

For the quarter, MCI said total revenues were $4.88 billion, up 8.7 percent from $4.49 billion. Core long distance business revenues were $4.4 billion, an increase of $334 million, or 8.2 percent from first quarter 1996 revenues.
It said first quarter traffic volumes grew four percent versus the same period a year ago.

During the first quarter MCI said its Business Markets unit posted double digit revenue growth, led by especially strong growth in value-added services such as data, Internet, conferencing and pre-paid calling cards.

Business services accounts for about two-thirds of the company's overall revenues. Virtual data services such as frame relay and asynchronous transfer mode more than doubled the revenues over the year ago quarter.
MCI, which is merging with British Telecommunications Plc in a $22 billion deal announced last October, said Internet revenues also doubled over the year ago quarter.

In its consumer business, MCI's MCI One brand, which pulls together a bundle of services on one bill, grew to more than two million customers of which 85 percent came from competitors, MCI said. MCI One was launched in April 1996.
MCI said its MCI One customers spend 10 percent more than average MCI customers, and are much more likely to subscribe to added value services like wireless and Internet.
MCI made strong progress in the emerging markets of medium distance, regional -- or IntraLATA -- calling, with volume of calls 50 percent higher than a year ago.

In local services, another new market for long distance carriers, MCI said revenues rose to $65 million from $40 million a year ago, with a 33 percent increase in revenues over the fourth quarter of 1996.
"As we move towards our merger with BT, MCI is focused on implementing long term strategies that position us for growth," MCI Chief Executive Gerald Taylor said.
"Our accelerated efforts in the local market are a perfect example of this strategy," he said.
MCI's share of losses at Concert, its global business venture with British Telecom fell to $6 million from $13 million in 1996's fourth quarter.
Information Technology revenues, which include MCI Systemhouse, the company's systems integration business, grew 27 percent to $433 million, with U.S. revenue doubling year-over-year.

It said first quarter revenues for ventures and developing markets grew 22 percent to $579 million and now account for 10 percent of the company's overall revenues. Such revenues were up 10 percent sequentially from the fourth quarter of 1996.

However, the net loss from ventures and developing markets rose to $103 million from $73 million in the fourth quarter. The wider loss cut MCI's core earnings of $0.57 per share by $0.15 to the reported overall figure of $0.42 per share.
It said total wireless revenue dropped to $75 million in the first quarter from $88 million a year ago, primarily due to the company's move to more selectively market its paging services.
Nonetheless, its wireless customer base grew to 425,000 customers from 373,000 in the first quarter 1996.
Increasingly, MCI wireless services are sold as part of an integrated package of services under its MCI One and networkMCI One customer plans.
MCI shares fell 1/4 point in early trading Thursday to 38-1/2 on volume of 840,000 shares.
-- Eric Auchard, New York newsdesk, 212-859-1736
